transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-02 14:30 UTC | Duration 45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (SE), Priya (SE), Carlos (CTO, Horizon), Anika (ML Eng), Jordan (PM), Samir (SRE)
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the account, Liam and Priya will do the console walkthrough.
00:18 Carlos: thanks, excited to see how tracing looks. we've been struggling with intermittent 5xxs that our prod alerts surface but can't root cause quickly.
00:32 Liam: yeah, totally. today we'll show tracing, error analysis, and request logs — how to go from an error surface to a specific failing prompt and kv cache behavior.
00:48 Jordan: quick note — our priority right now is debugging speed, second is cost, third is model isolation for PII.
01:05 Priya: noted. also will point out features that help with data residency and audit logs.
01:20 Anika: we run mixed workloads — low latency chat for customers and batch summarization for backfill — curious about per-route tracing.
01:35 Liam: Console supports per-route traces and token-level timing breakdowns. we'll open the tracing tab now.
01:52 [screen share starts]
02:10 Liam: here is the trace list — you can filter by route, model version, and status code. you see duration histogram on the right — quick way to spot tails.
02:30 Maya: small caveat — tracing sampling defaults to 10% for hosted, you can increase for a short window during a debug.
02:45 Samir: is that adjustable per-API key? we want to only sample problematic clients.
02:55 Liam: yes, per-route and per-api-key sampling, plus you can enable full traces for a time window.
03:10 Anika: what about sensitive payloads — is request body masked in logs?
03:18 Priya: by default we mask PII and have KMS-backed retention controls; you can opt into raw logs with extra permissions for SOC-approved users.
03:35 Carlos: can we export traces to our internal system? we use Datadog and a homegrown trace store.
03:45 Liam: exports are supported — streaming to third-party tracing systems or S3 for long term. note that exporting raw request bodies requires extra compliance review.
04:02 Jordan: show us a failure flow end-to-end, please.
04:12 Liam: sure. i'll pick a 500 error trace. you can see the waterfall: client -> routing -> model variant fallback -> inference engine timeout.
04:30 [pause, Liam clicks through steps]
04:45 Liam: the error analysis view links directly to request logs and to model execution timeline. notice the KV cache miss spike at 0.7s which correlates with token expansion and a downstream plugin call.
05:05 Anika: hmm that plugin call is our external ontology enrich, that could explain spikes when the plugin is slow. does Redwood annotate traces with third-party call latencies?
05:20 Liam: yes, if you instrument the plugin, Redwood tracing will surface external call spans. we also show CPU/GPU kernel timings on dedicated workers.
05:38 Carlos: are GPU kernel timings available for hosted?
05:45 Priya: limited for hosted; more granularity is available on Dedicated and Private where you can get per-kernel latency.
05:58 Maya: customer question: how do we search raw request logs for specific user IDs or prompts?
06:08 Liam: there's a query language — pretty similar to other log systems. you can search by correlation id, prompt hash, or user id. remember masked fields may require elevated permissions.
06:25 Jordan: any rate limit on request log retention?
06:30 Priya: retention tiers: 30d default, 90d/365d paid tiers, and archive to S3 for longer retention. audit logs are separate.
06:48 Samir: our compliance team will ask about KMS and HSM for keys.
06:55 Maya: note we integrate with customer KMS and support HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. that's usually part of the enterprise package.
07:10 Carlos: ok, show us the debugging flow for a slow tail — what are the steps from alert to mitigation?
07:22 Liam: common workflow: 1) alert points to increased latency on a route, 2) open tracing UI and filter by route/time, 3) identify slow spans (plugin/external calls, model fallback), 4) pivot to request logs to view payload and prompt, 5) create a diagnostic run (replay) or create a canary routing rule to shift traffic.
07:55 Anika: replay — how deterministic is that? we need to reproduce a failing prompt exactly.
08:03 Priya: you can replay the raw request with original headers and prompt. machine randomness can cause non-determinism, but model variants and seeds can be pinned for more reproducible runs.
08:25 Jordan: what about cost while replaying?
08:30 Maya: replay counts as normal inference usage — we suggest using a smaller model variant for repros when possible.
08:40 Liam: also we have a 'dry-run' mode to run through internal checks without full token billing, useful for validating routing logic.
08:55 Carlos: can we set automated alerts if KV cache miss rate exceeds X%?
09:03 Liam: yes — you can create metric alerts on cache hit/miss, latency percentiles, error rates.
09:20 Samir: what about multi-region fallbacks? if our primary region is overloaded, how are traces correlated?
09:30 Priya: traces carry a global request id so you can follow a request across regions, and the console shows aggregated spans per region.
09:45 Anika: we have a question about privacy — are request logs accessible to Redwood support engineers?
09:55 Maya: access is RBAC controlled; support can only see logs if customer grants support access or if account policies permit. We also have an audit trail for support access.
10:15 Jordan: ok cool. can you show the raw request log view?
10:22 [Liam navigates]
10:35 Liam: raw log view shows headers, prompt, model version, tokens, token timing, and error stack. there can be spellings in the transcriptions, sometimes names are off — small transcription note.
10:52 Carlos: I see some truncated payloads in the sample — is that because of masking or stream truncation?
11:00 Priya: usually masking or retention hooks truncate sensitive fields. full payloads are available if you enable raw logs with the right compliance add-on.
11:20 Anika: we'd like to bring a sample failing log after the call. what's the best way to share securely?
11:28 Maya: send via our secure intake form — we'll provide S3 upload link with presigned URL and KMS envelope encryption instructions.
11:40 Jordan: question on debugging runbook — do you have playbooks for common failures?
11:47 Liam: yes, we maintain a public runbook and a more detailed internal SE runbook; we'll share a trimmed version for the POC.
12:05 [short QA where customer asks about model variants and rollbacks]
12:25 Liam: for rollbacks we support canary and automatic fallback policies that route to a cheaper or older model if latency/SLOs breach.
12:40 Carlos: any latency SLOs you can point to?
12:45 Maya: for Dedicated we support SLA-backed latency tiers; hosted has published p50/p95 numbers per model on our docs. we'll include a benchmark sheet.
13:00 Anika: can you demo a failing request being triaged to a bug fix?
13:10 Liam: let's pick a trace with a model fallback. you can open the trace, click on the model execution timeline, and see the fallback reason — e.g., OOM or timeout.
13:35 [Liam simulates remedial route change]
13:50 Liam: after change, you can replay and compare traces side-by-side — console highlights differences in kernel timings and external call latencies.
14:10 Jordan: nice, that side-by-side will be helpful for our SREs.
14:25 Samir: about logs retention for private deployment — is it self-hosted?
14:33 Priya: Private can either store logs in customer-controlled S3 or in the deployer's storage. access is entirely customer controlled.
14:50 Carlos: what's the expected setup time for a trial with sample data?
14:58 Maya: we can spin a trial in 3-5 business days; if they want Dedicated capacity it takes longer.
15:10 Anika: for the POC success criteria — we want 1) reduce median time-to-detect by 50%, 2) reproduce and fix root cause for 3 reproducible errors, 3) validate tracing fidelity against Datadog.
15:30 Maya: agreed. we'll map those into the POC checklist.
15:45 Jordan: logs — is there a CLI to pull traces programmatically?
15:50 Liam: yes, our API supports exporting traces and request logs via CLI and SDKs.
16:05 Carlos: any blockers we foresee?
16:10 Maya: main items are security review and sample data redaction; we'll work with your security team.
16:22 [brief discussion on pricing and contractual timelines]
16:40 Maya: to recap next steps — we'll send pricing + SOC2 pack, Liam share runbook and sample traces, customer to upload a failing sample, and we schedule POC kickoff.
16:55 Anika: sounds good. thanks.
17:05 Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email.
17:12 [call ends]
